A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and corresponding material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original LDS evaluations, counterfactual retraining results, and attribution analyses on CIFAR-2, CIFAR-10, and ArtBench, including Figures 2–3 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains original attribution experiments and reports additional Hessian-approximation ablations and marginal-density evaluations, including Figures 5, 19, and 21.

M1.justification: The influence-function pipeline, curvature approximations, query batching, and gradient quantisation remain. EK-FAC was already introduced and evaluated in v3; v4 foregrounds it and calls it K-FAC Influence. The expanded derivations and evaluations of existing design options do not establish a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image attribution using CIFAR-2, CIFAR-10, and ArtBench. ArtBench's expanded description is not a new dataset addition. Uniform dequantisation, alternative measurements, and training-set-size sweeps change preprocessing and evaluation settings within the retained coverage.

E2.justification: TRAK, D-TRAK, CLIP similarity, and exact retraining remain. Figure 2a drops the separate ordinary K-FAC row while retaining EK-FAC under the renamed K-FAC Influence label. New Appendix C.3 comparisons evaluate additional combinations of empirical/model Fisher, expand/reduce, and eigenvalue correction.

E3.justification: V4 introduces marginal-density evaluation on uniformly dequantised CIFAR and training-size sweeps from 10 to 25,000 examples. New Hessian ablations specify matched computation budgets, including 125 samples each for EK-FAC eigenbasis and eigenvalues. ArtBench's stated LDS design changes from v3's universal 100-subset specification to 50 subsets; this establishes a reporting revision, not necessarily rerunning.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a controlled ablation of Fisher choice, expand/reduce approximation, and eigenvalue correction. V4 also expands distribution-stability analysis across training-set sizes and adds likelihood damping sensitivity. V3's gradient-sample-count sweep is removed. Compression and timestep/downweighting analyses remain, although several results are updated.

E5.justification: V3 Appendix K.5 reports 500 retrained models for every LDS benchmark. V4 Appendix J.6 specifies 250 for ArtBench, arising from 50 subsets with five seeds each. This revises reported retraining counts; five-seed averaging and standard-error reporting otherwise remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Matching the EK-FAC variant, Figure 2 loss LDS changes from 27.4%/23.2% to 26.7%/22.6% on CIFAR-2/10. New Figure 21 reports marginal-density LDS of 21.6% for K-FAC Influence using loss versus 14.9% for D-TRAK; these replace a different trajectory-probability evaluation. Ablation, timestep, and removal results also change. In v4 Figure 3, CIFAR-10 with 2% removal gives 0.00067 for K-FAC Influence versus 0.00079 for D-TRAK.

T1.justification: Equations (8) and (11) correct the empirical-Fisher decomposition from log/exp(loss) to negative-log/exp(negative loss). Appendix B replaces the score-based derivation with a random-vector second-moment derivation. Appendix C revises the weight-sharing formulation and adds explicit diffusion-specific expand/reduce derivations, substantially extending the mathematical treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal introduction/discussion claims remain: a scalable influence-function framework unifying earlier approaches, improved attribution performance, and limitations in predicting numerical counterfactual changes. Explicitly foregrounding EK-FAC does not introduce a contribution absent from v3.

C2.justification: The overall caution about numerical attribution remains. Observation 3 shifts from ELBO stability to marginal-density stability, with a more explicit training-size threshold interpretation. Appendix C.3 adds rank-related explanations for the ablation results while acknowledging that Hessian approximation quality was not directly measured. The trajectory-specific failure explanation is removed.

D1.justification: V4 fills substantial documentation gaps for existing ArtBench experiments: image resolution, latent diffusion architecture, frozen Stable Diffusion 2 autoencoder, sampling, training iterations, optimiser, learning rate, warm-up, clipping, and EMA settings. It also adds a project source-code link and autodifferentiation guidance. These disclosures do not establish that the underlying ArtBench method changed.

R1.justification: V4 adds references to Dangel et al. (2025), Liao et al. (2022), and Rombach et al. (2022). Related work adds emphasis on damping's contribution to earlier D-TRAK results and condenses the separate K-FAC/EK-FAC history. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Evaluation definitions move from v3 Appendix D into Section 4. Appendix C is subdivided into background, derivation, and ablation sections, and sampling receives a separate subsection. Terminology and several paragraphs are edited, but most of the main narrative and appendix structure remain recognisable.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially revised: new Hessian-ablation and likelihood-sensitivity figures appear; v3's correlation matrices are replaced by a multipanel size-sweep display with generated images; and trajectory-result plots are replaced by marginal-density plots. Figure 2's row structure changes, and main figures are relocated. The runtime and memory tables remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens support for its central design choices through controlled Hessian ablations and explicit weight-sharing derivations, corrects the empirical-Fisher sign error, and fills important ArtBench reproducibility gaps. Marginal-density experiments provide more direct evidence for the attribution question. The retained claim of consistently superior removal results is now overstated by Figure 3, but this limited inconsistency does not outweigh the substantial gains in justification and documentation.
